audiences.name: Students
audiences.free: Start on the Free page. Use a free tier for practice, and move to a paid plan only when the limit blocks the assignment.
audiences.caution: Do not turn in generated work as your own. Follow your school's rules on academic integrity.

audiences.name: Developers
audiences.free: The open-weights pick on the coding page can run on your own machine. A hosted free tier is for drafts, not for secrets.
audiences.caution: Do not paste secrets, private keys, or unreleased source into a chat that trains on chats by default.

audiences.name: Small businesses
audiences.free: Use the free option on the Free page for a first draft. Pay when you need the leader for the job you do every day.
audiences.caution: Do not invent a price, a review, or a result a customer did not have.

audiences.name: Writers and marketers
audiences.free: The writing category's open-weights pick is the free starting point. The leader is the paid starting point.
audiences.caution: Do not publish a claim you have not checked, and say when a draft was generated.

audiences.name: Lawyers
audiences.free: A free tier is a poor place for client work. If the document cannot leave your network, use the open-weights pick and run it yourself.
audiences.caution: This is not legal advice. Do not paste client-confidential documents into a chat that trains on chats by default.

audiences.name: Researchers
audiences.free: Use the research category's open-weights pick when the stack has to be downloadable. Otherwise start with the free tier and open every source.
audiences.caution: Open the sources. A citation can point at a page that does not say what the draft claims.
